mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior month reduces discount rates applied to corporate earnings forecasts, lowering the present value of future cash flows and thus depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% in the preceding month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a similar rate-neutral period (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than during periods of similar labor market dynamics but neutral wage growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 2% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating economic demand, prompting firms to raise capital expenditures and expand output, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO grows by > 2% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Five-day forward returns are negative despite INDPRO exceeding 2% growth for the required period (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the ratio of import prices (CPIAUCSL) to GDP deflator (not in catalog - so use CPIAUCSL alone) over two consecutive months suggests weaker inflationary pressures, allowing the Federal Reserve to maintain a steady policy stance and preserving investor optimism, resulting in positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by > 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in a regression controlling for inflation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, it indicates a tightening cycle that raises real discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of confirmed tightening (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% followed by a sustained increase in labor participation (PAYEMS) suggests a demographic or confidence-driven expansion in the labor force, which can support economic growth and equity valuations, yielding positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and PAYEMS increases by > 50,000 in the following month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the described labor indicators (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence proxies (not available - so use HOUST as a demand proxy) above historical averages for the prior quarter is associated with higher corporate earnings expectations and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 120 and HOUST > 2000 for the prior quarter
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when both proxies are above threshold (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS declines below 2%, the central bank's accommodative stance lowers the real risk-free rate, enhancing the present value of equity cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by 0.5% monthly for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during comparable periods of neutral policy (p > 0.05).
